title: Rate-adaptive burst manager and request-fairness guards
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem statement:
Customers using Dedicated pools occasionally hit short-lived demand spikes that should be absorbed by transient capacity, but current behavior leads to: unfair throttling across tenants in the same fleet, unexpected overage charges when short spikes exceed billing windows, and poor tail latency for latency-sensitive routes. We need a rate-adaptive burst manager that coordinates surge pools, enforces per-request fairness, and exposes clear invoiceable events to downstream billing and notifications.

Goals:
- Smooth short spikes without violating per-tenant throughput guarantees for reserved capacity.
- Apply a fairness policy that prevents a single noisy tenant from consuming transient capacity to the detriment of peers.
- Produce deterministic, debuggable billing signals for temporary boosts and overage events.
- Integrate with existing autoscaling controllers and policy UI in Console.

Scope/Out of scope:
- In scope: allocation algorithm, request-level admission checks, burst metering events, billing signal schema, operator runbook, small Console UX to visualize active boosts.
- Out of scope: wholesale pricing changes, long-term reserved capacity adjustments, changes to model-level token accounting.

Proposed design (summary):
1) Admission window: each fleet maintains a short sliding window (configurable, default 30s) for transient capacity allocation. Requests declare a request-class (latency-sensitive | best-effort) and expected P99 latency budget.
2) Weighted fair share across tenants: transient capacity is allocated proportionally to each tenant's reserved allocation within the fleet, capped by a per-tenant burst budget and a configurable max-in-flight fraction.
3) Rate-adaptive throttling: when transient capacity pressure is high, the burst manager rate-limits best-effort requests first using a token-bucket that refills based on observed smoothing factor; latency-sensitive requests get preferential but bounded access.
4) Metering events & billing hooks: emit structured events for start/end of a tenant's transient boost, volume of transient tokens consumed, and an overage flag when consumption crosses a billing threshold. These map to billing pipeline tags and invoice lines.
5) Fallbacks: if the manager or surge pool is unavailable, fall back to static per-tenant caps to avoid uncontrolled overage.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit + integration tests for admission logic and fairness invariants exist and pass.
- Simulated multi-tenant load tests show: a noisy tenant does not reduce other tenants' throughput below 95% of baseline reserved capacity during short spikes.
- Billing events emitted match consumption within 2% in synthetic trace tests.
- Console dashboard shows active boosts and per-tenant transient consumption.
- Documentation and operator runbook published with rollback steps.

Implementation plan (phases):
A) Design and prototyping (this ticket): final algorithm, event schema, operator runbook draft, Console mock.
B) Core runtime impl: burst manager service + admission hooks in serving agents; lightweight surge pool allocator.
C) Billing pipeline integration: map events to invoiceable metrics and update billing reconciler.
D) Canary rollout on a small Dedicated fleet, monitor SLOs and billing reconciliation.

Rollout & Monitoring:
- Key metrics: transient_tokens_consumed, boost_start_count, boost_duration_p50/p95/p99, per-tenant_reserved_utilization, overage_event_count.
- Alerts: unexpected increase in overage_event_count or drop in reserved utilization >5% sustained for 5m.
- Canary to 5% of fleets for 48 hours, then 25% for a week before full rollout.

Notes and trade-offs:
- Simplicity vs optimality: strict proportional fairness is easy to reason about but may under-utilize capacity when tenants are idle; we add a small opportunistic floor to improve utilization.
- Billing granularity: finer-grained metering increases accuracy but also billed event volume and reconciliation complexity. We choose 30s aggregation for an initial balance.

Links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/RA-Burst-Manager-Design
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1287
- Billing schema proposal: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c-billing-schema

Deliverables for this ticket:
- Draft design doc updated with final parameters.
- Event schema JSON file (in repo) and mapping spreadsheet for billing.
- Operator runbook draft.
- Console mock screenshots attached.

2026-03-06 - Marco: Integrated admission hook into serving-agent; ran local e2e with k6 load which reproduced fairness guarantees. Observed small latency bump for best-effort traffic under extreme pressure — acceptable per SLO.
2026-03-09 - Ops: Runbook draft added. Contains steps to disable burst manager per-fleet (kill switch), how to inspect active boosts, and reconciliation checklist for disputed invoices.
